review_basis.reviewed_scope: Root R11 proposal received 2026-10-19, before code freeze; no frozen R11 DESIGN.md was present at review time.
review_basis.card: H-NF19-17 — Frequently sample informative updates while preserving risk

fixed_comparison.model: FP32 224→64 GELU, two-target mean output plus unused variance head; same byte-identical initialization and fit-only normalizer in both arms.

arms.importance: With replacement, p_i=0.5/N + 0.5*g_i/sum_j(g_j), where g_i is the exact joint two-target shared-parameter data-loss gradient norm for row i at the common initial parameters theta0.

fixed_comparison.importance_correction: For each sampled row multiply its row loss by 1/(N*p_i), then take the batch mean. The mixture floor implies 1/(N*p_i) <= 2.
fixed_comparison.common_rng_coupling: Both arms consume the same uniform variates and invert their respective CDFs; different row sequences are intentional. This is a reproducible coupling, not same-example pairing.

draw_budget.batch_partition_per_round: 62 batches of 512 plus one final batch of 64
draw_budget.label: 756 fixed update steps; do not call this 12 epochs of unique-row coverage.

objective_and_unbiasedness.fixed_weight_denominator: mu_w = (1/N) * sum_i sum_t w_it, where w_it is the canonical fit mask times abs(clip(y_it,-2,2)).
objective_and_unbiasedness.estimator: Each update averages sampled l_i(theta)/(N*p_i). Its expectation is the gradient of the globally normalized pooled WMSE at fixed theta, before clipping.
objective_and_unbiasedness.gradient_norm_scope: g_i is the norm of the joint two-target gradient over shared trunk and mean-head parameters for the same fixed per-row pooled-loss contribution; do not sum separate target norms or substitute a row-normalized/unweighted proxy. The unused variance head contributes zero.
objective_and_unbiasedness.analytic_GELU_norm_for_tiny_autograd_che: For exact GELU, a=W1*x+b1; h=GELU(a); mu=W2*h+b2; u_t=2*w_t*(mu_t-y_t)/mu_w; delta=(W2^T*u) elementwise-multiplied by GELU'(a), where GELU'(a)=Phi(a)+a*phi(a). Then grad(W2)=u outer h, grad(b2)=u, grad(W1)=delta outer x, grad(b1)=delta; g_i is the Euclidean norm of these joint gradients. Exclude decoupled AdamW weight decay from g_i. Compare this formula with tiny autograd before admission.

interpretation_boundary.primary_allowed_claim: A conditional final pooled-WP difference after exactly 756 successful updates per arm on the fixed exposed R3 panel.
interpretation_boundary.prepass_cost_requirement: Measure and report gradient-norm prepass and each arm wall/CPU time. This fixed-step design does not test lower total cost or equal-wall-clock advantage; do not claim a practical efficiency win.
interpretation_boundary.nonlinear_optimizer_limit: Importance correction makes the preclip stochastic gradient estimator unbiased at fixed theta. Global norm clipping and AdamW make optimizer updates/trajectories nonlinear, so no unbiased full-trajectory or final-model claim follows.
interpretation_boundary.panel_limit: R3 is an exposed/adaptive panel, not a fresh holdout; inference is conditional on this panel. Do not treat the 32 evaluation components as independent training replications or make generalization/public-score claims.
interpretation_boundary.selection_limit: No R7 outcomes may determine R11 seed, learning schedule, draw count, architecture, correction, stopping point, or any other hyperparameter; no tuning on the R3 evaluation scores.

pre_admission_falsifiers_and_gates: Tiny autograd agrees with the analytic joint per-example GELU gradient norm, including weights and the fixed mu_w denominator.

On a deterministic tiny fixture, importance-weighted batch gradient expectation matches the full pooled-WMSE gradient; verify probability normalization, correction bound <=2, and same-uniform reproducibility.
Fit-only rows/targets alone define mu_w, gradient norms, and p_i; evaluation arrays or scores never enter them.
Both arms use the same initialization, features/normalizer, FP32 mode, and fixed optimizer settings; exactly 756 successful steps per arm are required for a paired endpoint.

Report p_i/importance-weight range and effective sample concentration, plus preclip norm/clipping incidence. These diagnose the tested sampler but do not prove lower gradient variance or equal-time efficiency.
If either arm fails to complete all 756 steps under the authorized 0.5 CPU / 1.4 GB high / 1.5 GB max / 600 s cap, record an incomplete pair and make no predictive comparison.
falsifier: If the importance arm does not improve fixed-step pooled WP, close this exact fixed initial-gradient sampler on this panel. If it does improve, treat it as a recipe-level, fixed-step result only; measured prepass/runtime cost can still negate practical value.
review_limits: Design-only review. No R11 code, data arrays, model, fit, or remote resource was accessed.
